An infinitely long straight wire carries a current $i_1=1$ amp. A rectangular current loop placed in the same plane of shown dimensions carries a current $i_2=1$ amp anticlockwise. Magnitude of net force on the loop is found to be $\beta\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}$. Find value of $\beta$.

(Given: $a=3$ m, $d=4$ m, $qB=0.8$ C-Tesla)

\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P2-PHY-S2-Q04, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=2, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Force on charges}, answer={6.02 to 6.03}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S3 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: momentum conservation, circular motion in a magnetic field | steps: equal and opposite momenta; angular speeds in ratio 24; both circles are tangent at the origin; meeting condition; solve theta | I: the particles meet again at the origin}]
A neutral atom of atomic mass number 100 which is stationary at the origin in gravity free space emits an $\alpha$-particle ($A$) in $z$-direction. The product ion is $P$. A uniform magnetic field exists in the $x$-direction. Disregard the electro magnetic interaction between $A$ and $P$. If the angle of rotation of $A$ after which $A$ and $P$ will meet for the first time is $\theta$ radians, what is the value of $\theta$?
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS12-P2-PHY-S1-Q02, source={TOAS - Test 12 (10 Jul 2022)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Force on wires}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S2 I0 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: force on a segment due to two parallel wires | steps: field of each wire along the segment; force on a current element; integrate over the length}]
A straight segment OP of length $L$ of a circuit carrying current $I$ ampere is placed along x-axis. Two infinitely long straight wires A and B each extending from $z=-\infty$ to $+\infty$ are fixed at $y=-\ell$ meter and $y=+\ell$ meter respectively. Wires A and B, each carry current $I$ ampere along positive z-axis. Given that O is origin of the coordinate system. The magnitude of force on segment OP is :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{\mu_0}{\pi}I^2\ln\left(1+\dfrac{L^2}{\ell^2}\right)$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}I^2\ln\left(1+\dfrac{L^2}{\ell^2}\right)$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{\mu_0}{\pi}I^2\ln\left(1+\dfrac{\ell^2}{L^2}\right)$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}I^2\ln\left(1+\dfrac{\ell^2}{L^2}\right)$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{center}\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
\begin{tabular}{|L{3.4cm}|L{1.5cm}|L{1.5cm}|}
\hline
\multicolumn{1}{|c|}{Column-1}&\multicolumn{1}{c|}{Column-2}&\multicolumn{1}{c|}{Column-3}\\\hline
(I) Positive charge with $\vec V=\dfrac{2E_0}{B_0}\hat i$.&(i) $\vec E=E_0\hat j$&(P) $\vec B=-B_0\hat k$\\\hline
(II) Negative charge with $\vec V=\dfrac{E_0}{B_0}(\hat j+\hat k)$.&(ii) $\vec E=E_0\hat i$&(Q) $\vec B=B_0\hat i$\\\hline
(III) Positive charge with $\vec V=\dfrac{E_0}{B_0}(\hat i+\hat j)$.&(iii) $\vec E=E_0\hat k$&(R) $\vec B=-B_0\hat j$\\\hline

\end{tabular}\end{center}
